# Kyoto 4-Day Spring Itinerary for 2 Adults

A balanced Kyoto plan for **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-13** with temples, food markets, one relaxing activity, and **public-transit-first routing**. I’ve kept each day to roughly **under 8 km walking** and aimed to stay within your **JPY 180,000 total budget excluding flights**.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Plan

| Day | Focus | Key Stops | Est. Cost for 2 | Walking |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Day 1 | Higashiyama temples + classic Kyoto streets | Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka, Gion, Yasaka Shrine | JPY 22,000–28,000 | 6–7 km |
| Day 2 | Central Kyoto food + markets | Nishiki Market, Teramachi, Kyoto Imperial Palace area | JPY 20,000–26,000 | 4–6 km |
| Day 3 | Arashiyama + relaxing soak | Bamboo Grove, Tenryu-ji, river area, onsen/spa | JPY 28,000–40,000 | 5–7 km |
| Day 4 | Northern temples + indoor backup flexibility | Kinkaku-ji, Ryoan-ji, optional museum/cafe time | JPY 18,000–24,000 | 5–7 km |

## Kyoto Day Plan

### Day 1: Higashiyama Temple Loop
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Start early at **Kiyomizu-dera** to avoid crowds; continue through **Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka**.
- **Afternoon:** Walk or short-bus to **Yasaka Shrine** and the **Gion** area for tea, photos, and a slower pace.
- **Food:** Lunch near Higashiyama; try yudofu, soba, or a set meal in a small local restaurant.
- **Transit tip:** Use buses sparingly here; a short taxi between Kiyomizu and Gion can save time and walking.
- **Estimated cost:** Admissions, lunch, drinks, local transit for 2: **JPY 22,000–28,000**.

### Day 2: Nishiki Market and Central Kyoto
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- **Morning:** Explore **Nishiki Market** for snacks and lunch bites; go early for the best selection.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Morning:** Explore **Nishiki Market** for snacks and lunch bites; go early for the best selection, Kyoto, Japan
- **Afternoon:** Browse **Teramachi** and **Shinkyogoku** shopping arcades, then unwind at a cafe.
- **Food:** Build a shared tasting lunch from tamagoyaki, tofu skin, pickles, seafood skewers, and sweets.
- **Transit tip:** This day is easiest by **subway + walking**; central Kyoto is compact and transit-friendly.
- **Estimated cost:** Market food, cafe stop, local transit for 2: **JPY 20,000–26,000**.

### Day 3: Arashiyama and a Relaxing Soak
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Take the train to **Arashiyama** and visit the **Bamboo Grove** early.
- **Afternoon:** See **Tenryu-ji**, then slow down by the river or add the **Sagano scenic area** if energy is good.
- **Food:** Have a riverside lunch or a tofu-based set meal; keep the pace leisurely.
- **Relaxing activity:** Book a **sentō, spa, or onsen-style bath** in the late afternoon or evening.
- **Transit tip:** Use **JR or Hankyu** depending on your hotel location; avoid buses at peak return hours.
- **Estimated cost:** Transit, temple entry, lunch, spa/onsen for 2: **JPY 28,000–40,000**.

### Day 4: Northern Kyoto Temples
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Kinkaku-ji** early, then continue to **Ryoan-ji**.
- **Afternoon:** Keep the rest flexible for a cafe, bookstore, or a museum if you want a lighter final day.
- **Food:** Lunch near the northern temple area or back in central Kyoto for better variety.
- **Transit tip:** This area is best by **bus + short taxi**; it is less walkable than central Kyoto.
- **Estimated cost:** Admissions, transit, lunch for 2: **JPY 18,000–24,000**.

## Budget Fit and Transit Strategy

- **Target total for 4 days:** **JPY 88,000–118,000**
- That leaves a comfortable buffer inside your **JPY 180,000** cap for nicer meals, extra admissions, or a better spa.
- Best transit mix:
  - **Subway + JR** for longer cross-city moves
  - **Bus** only for temple-heavy areas
Media: Alt=Bus** only for temple-heavy areas, Kyoto, Japan
  - **Taxi** for 1–2 short hops to reduce walking and save energy
- To stay under **8 km walking/day**, cluster nearby sights and avoid adding extra shrine stops on the same day.

## Rainy-Day Backup Plan

If one day turns wet, swap in this indoor-focused route:

- **Morning:** **Kyoto Railway Museum** or **Kyoto National Museum**
- **Afternoon:** **Nishiki Market** covered arcade + **Teramachi/Shinkyogoku** shopping streets
- **Late afternoon:** Long cafe break, dessert stop, or a department-store food hall
- **Evening:** Optional spa/onsen or a seated kaiseki dinner

Why this works:
- Most of the day stays **indoors or under arcade cover**
- Transit remains simple by **subway, train, and short taxi**
- Walking stays moderate even in bad weather
